A draft in one go, and watching anything on its own

2026-10-22 · What changed is circled in red. Taken from the running app on episode #4, after the change; the two "before" shots were taken first.

Make it all: a draft to watch, or the finished video

"Make it all" now asks which to end on. A draft to watch records the voices, draws the pictures still wanted, then builds the quick preview and opens the Export step, so the episode can be watched through before anything is rendered at full size. One button with a choice, because the header has no room for a second button beside the episode title. Both batches now stop drawing rather than spend more than the cost shown; this episode needs no new pictures, so the dialog says so and leaves that sentence out.

Watch one clip on its own

A play button appears on a clip's card under the pointer, and Watch clip sits beside Audition audio in the inspector (Ctrl+Shift+P). The clip plays small, with its own sound, in a player beside its card. It reuses the quick preview's drawing of the clip, so after a preview it is instant; before one, only that clip is drawn.

Editing keys on the preview

L plays, and pressed again plays at twice then four times the speed; K pauses; J slows a fast play down, or steps five seconds back; comma and full stop step one frame while paused. The clock shows the speed when it is not normal, and clicking the picture plays or pauses it.

Not shown

Each teaser card also gains a play button and a Fill the frame switch (crop to the upright frame instead of the blurred background). Teaser cards appear only after Suggest teasers, which is a paid request to the script service, so they were not opened for these shots. The draft they play is covered by an FFmpeg test.
